query_text: What medicine should I take when I get a cold?

message.content:
Based on information from health authorities, here is guidance on what to take when you have a cold:

## Important First Points

- **There is no cure for the common cold** — it is caused by viruses, so antibiotics will not help and should not be used.
- Most colds improve on their own within **7–10 days**.
- Treatment focuses on **relieving symptoms** while your body recovers.

## Over-the-Counter Medicines by Symptom

| Symptom | Recommended Medicine | Notes |
|---------|----------------------|-------|
| **Fever, headache, sore throat, body aches** | Acetaminophen (Tylenol) or Ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin) | Do not exceed recommended doses. Check that other cold medicines don't already contain these to avoid accidental overdose. |
| **Stuffy nose / congestion** | Decongestants (pseudoephedrine, phenylephrine) or decongestant nasal sprays (Afrin, Neo-Synephrine) | Nasal sprays should not be used for more than **3 days** to avoid rebound congestion. Decongestants can raise blood pressure and heart rate. |
| **Runny nose / sneezing** | Antihistamines (Benadryl, Chlor-Trimeton) | May cause drowsiness; non-sedating options are available. Not very effective for cold symptoms in some cases. |
| **Cough** | Cough suppressants, expectorants, or honey (for adults and children over 1 year) | Evidence for cough medicines is mixed; they may not work significantly better than placebo. |

## Non-Drug Remedies That Help

- **Rest** and plenty of sleep
- **Drink lots of fluids** (water, warm broths)
- **Humidifier or steam** from a hot shower
- **Saline nasal spray or rinses** (Neti pot)
- **Warm salt water gargle** for sore throat
- **Hot lemon and honey drink** (not for children under 1 year)

## Important Warnings

- **Children under 6:** Avoid decongestant nasal sprays/drops and most OTC cough/cold medicines. Use only children-strength acetaminophen or ibuprofen for fever, with correct dosing.
- **Never give aspirin to children or teenagers** — risk of Reye's syndrome.
- **Avoid zinc nasal sprays** — FDA warns they may cause permanent loss of smell.
- **Check combination medicines** carefully so you don't double up on ingredients like acetaminophen, which can cause liver damage in excess.
- **If you have high blood pressure, heart disease, or other chronic conditions**, consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking decongestants.

## When to See a Doctor

- Fever lasting more than 3–4 days
- Symptoms lasting more than 10 days without improvement
- Trouble breathing, chest pain, or severe shortness of breath
- Symptoms that improve then worsen
- Severe dehydration
- If you have a weakened immune system or chronic medical conditions

If you're unsure which medicine is right for you, especially if you take other medications or have health conditions, consult a pharmacist or healthcare provider.

---

Sources:
1. https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/common-cold/
2. https://www.cdc.gov/common-cold/treatment/index.html
3. https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/common-cold/diagnosis-treatment/drc-20351611
4. https://www.webmd.com/cold-and-flu/decongestants-antihistamines-cold
5. https://www.webmd.com/cold-and-flu/cold-medicine-treatment-when-what-how
